# Conditional Process Plan

Shared planning logic that adds a conditional payment-action gate to an inherited Connections plan. It produces contract and state declarations; producing a plan does not itself execute or complete a payment.

`clauseKey` identifies the candidate configuration at `/clauseRuntime/work/candidate/<clauseKey>`. The hooks `requestPolicy`, `policyAction`, `policyWatches` and `requestStep(gate, policy)` have no implementation here. They supply the policy, action name, additional watched paths and subsequent request step; this type alone does not establish their values, actors or payment effects.

## Conditional gate

`plan` obtains the policy and calls `planConnections`. Only policy `mode: "when"` adds conditional behavior. An absent `mode` defaults to `"workflow"` for this decision; every other mode returns the inherited plan unchanged.

For `mode: "when"`:

- `parameters/sources` on the candidate defaults to `{}` and declares aliases used by the policy's `when` expression.
- `/paymentProcess_<clauseKey>/<action>Allowed`, with `<action>` supplied by `policyAction`, is planned with initial value `false`.
- `/paymentTerms/<action>Gate` is set to that gate's path, preserving the other `/paymentTerms` fields. An existing different gate reference rejects planning with `PAYMENT_POLICY_GATE_CONFLICT`.
- Each path from `policyWatches` and each document path discovered in `when` receives a Document Update Channel and sequential handler. Nonempty `parameters/sources` also adds an Embedded Node Channel named `paymentSources` with the same handler steps.

When one of these handlers runs, it evaluates permission as true only if `/activation/active` equals `true`, either `/clauses/documentSources` is absent or `/sourceLinks/ready` equals `true`, and the policy's `when` expression equals `true`. It replaces the gate value only when it differs, then runs the step returned by `requestStep`. That step is not restricted here to false-to-true changes. Its own request conditions and effects remain unspecified.

These paths belong to the document where the generated contracts execute, including a nested document when applicable. The gate records conditional eligibility, not payment completion or a viewer's permission. Its planned initial `false` does not imply that an absent stored value is false, and planning does not immediately evaluate the predicate.

## Predicate constraints

`when` must have statically discoverable, pure dependencies. The scanner accepts `$document`, `$eq`, `$ne`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$and`, `$or`, `$not`, `$exists`, `$includes`, `$size`, `$add`, `$subtract`, `$literal`, and the operand keys `list` and `val`. It traverses lists and objects but does not inspect `$literal` contents.

Every `$document` operand must be literal text beginning with `/` and different from `/`; computed paths are rejected. A path beginning `/sources/<alias>` requires that alias in `parameters/sources`. Unsupported keys, invalid paths and undeclared aliases reject planning with `PAYMENT_PREDICATE_REQUIRES_STATIC_PURE_DEPENDENCIES`, `PAYMENT_PREDICATE_STATIC_PATH_REQUIRED` and `PAYMENT_PREDICATE_SOURCE_NOT_DECLARED`, respectively. Traversal remaining after 33 scan rounds rejects with `PAYMENT_PREDICATE_TOO_DEEP`.

## Inherited connection behavior

`planConnections` merges `type/defaultBindings` with candidate `bindings`. Property bindings must be declared in `type/bindingTypes`; they are required unless listed in `type/optionalBindings`. A `pointer` binding must be non-root text beginning with `/`; other bindings must match their declared kind. Clause, action and connection names must be nonempty and contain no `.`, `/` or `~`.

Actions come from `type/actions`, or `parameters/actions` when `type/configurableActions` equals `true`. A structural `type/initialState` can support a clause without actions. Each action binding is a dictionary of named connections. An action's `automatic` connection uses the reserved name `_automatic`; `pathBinding` resolves through property bindings.

Connection `on` supports `workflow`, `event`, `channel`, `change`, `embedded`, `collection`, `initialized`, `activated` and `timer`. Source-specific fields are checked; unsupported fields and duplicate workflow names reject planning. Workflow connections use `party`, falling back to `channel`, and require a valid authenticated-channel name; `request` and `event` can constrain calls. Change and embedded sources require non-root `path` values. Collection handlers check that the event's `sourcePath` lies below their configured path. Embedded and collection sources request embedding unless `embed` is explicitly `false`; `type/embeds` and `type/embedsCollections` also contribute declared pointer bindings.

On an eligible trigger, action `defaults` are merged with connection `params`. Connection `when` defaults to `true` and skips execution when unsatisfied. Declared `args`, action `require/when`, and `parameters/conditions/<action>` are then checked; failed requirements reject execution. Conditions may name only declared actions. Optional `preflight` precedes connection `before`, action `do`, and connection `after`.

A preflight must set `actionResult/outcome` to `acceptedNew`, `duplicate`, `rejected` or `skipped`; only `acceptedNew` continues. Actions with `resultContract: "outcome-v1"` must likewise return an explicit outcome, and only `acceptedNew` reaches `after`. The default `resultContract` is `"legacy"`. Connection `once` defaults to `false`; when true, reaching the end sets `fired`, suppressing later executions. Connection state starts with `armed: false` and `fired: false` at `/connectionState_<clauseKey>/<action>.<connection>`; these flags do not confirm external success.

`type/snapshotBindings` captures existing bound values during planning and rejects missing snapshots. Parameters are captured without `actions` and `conditions`, unless `type/readParametersFromDocument` is true, in which case captured parameters are `{}`. `type/initialState` contributes object state at declared pointer bindings.

Timer connections require exactly one of `timestamp` or `afterEvent`. Absolute `timestamp` is an integer Unix time in microseconds from 0 through 9007199254740991 and forbids `delayMs` and `policy`. Relative timers require a timestamped source other than initialization and positive integer `delayMs` up to 9007199254740. Their `policy` defaults to `"first"`, which suppresses arming after `armed` becomes true; `"latest"` permits another request. `cancelOn` must name a source and emits cancellation for the keyed timer. Cancellation does not reset `armed` here. Timer requests and cancellation requests do not themselves prove firing or an external outcome.

`validateConfiguration` calls inherited configuration validation and `requestPolicy`; detailed connection checks occur during planning. `validateTransition` always returns `allowed: false` with `PAYMENT_PROCESS_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`.

Concrete request behavior is left to the unimplemented hooks; an allowed gate or emitted request does not establish a completed payment.
